fields.v: No SDD tool. Four handoff views (no versions): (1) Repository only (baseline: checkpointed repo + original task prompt); (2) Raw trace (predecessor event log up to the checkpoint); (3) Summary notes (free-form natural-language notes generated by the predecessor-side model); (4) Structured notes (authors' fixed-field 'bounded continuation contract')

Structured handoff note with deterministic fields (repository change state, changed source files, non-source artifacts, validation outcome after latest source change, latest validation command, latest validation evidence, continuation-state label) and model-generated fields (problem understanding, work completed, evidence observed, observed failures, remaining uncertainty, rollback notes, recommended next action). Summary notes: free text (investigation, edits, validation attempts, uncertainty, next steps). Raw trace: event history

Predecessor agent (Qwen) works on a SWE-bench task -> interrupted at a deterministic handoff point (after first source edit / after first validation result / after first post-failure edit) -> repository frozen -> handoff view generated (notes by predecessor-side model, temperature 0, 1,600-token cap) -> successor agent takes over with the view + original prompt -> official SWE-bench validation
None (fully automated; takeover prompt tells successor to verify handoff text, not to trust it)
Single artefact (handoff context given to a successor agent: none, raw trace, summary notes or structured note)
Not classifiable (no specification; authors' wording: handoff as 'bounded continuation contract')
Existing code base: resuming interrupted SWE-bench Verified issue-resolution tasks (bug fixes in open-source Python repos)

N/A (no human participants; agent-to-agent handoff)

Agent events (OpenHands trajectory records: LLM actions + tool observations), cumulative prompt tokens (primary cost metrics); first-prompt size in characters. Completion tokens and wall-clock time logged but not used; note-generation cost excluded
Official SWE-bench resolution (solved rate) after takeover; breakdown by handoff point and handoff state (needs completion / already solved; preserve / existing behavior broken)

None

Automatic: OpenHands logs, official SWE-bench harness; bootstrap CIs (5,000 resamples) and McNemar tests. Manual inspection for failure modes

Agent = OpenHands-style runtime (native tool calling disabled; 4 h timeout, 500 steps) for all; predecessor Qwen3.6-27B. Criterion: official SWE-bench resolution; cost = median agent events and prompt tokens per takeover (local vLLM serving, no money cost). Values: solved rate; median events; median prompt tokens (Table 2). Main study (181 runs each):
- Repository only + OpenHands + Qwen3.6-27B (baseline): 46.4%; 99 events; 1.63M tokens
- Raw trace + OpenHands + Qwen3.6-27B: 52.5% (+6.1 pp, p=0.035); 41 (-59%); 811k (-50%)
- Summary notes + OpenHands + Qwen3.6-27B: 51.4% (+5.0, p=0.093); 53 (-46%); 602k (-63%)
- Structured notes + OpenHands + Qwen3.6-27B: 50.8% (+4.4, p=0.134); 55 (-44%); 660k (-60%)
- Repository only + OpenHands + gemma-4-31B-it (baseline): 42.5%; 49; 738k
- Raw trace + OpenHands + gemma-4-31B-it: 49.2% (+6.6, p=0.029); 21 (-57%); 300k (-59%)
- Summary notes + OpenHands + gemma-4-31B-it: 44.2% (+1.7, p=0.678); 33 (-33%); 319k (-57%)
- Structured notes + OpenHands + gemma-4-31B-it: 43.6% (+1.1, p=0.815); 39 (-20%); 317k (-57%)
- Repository only + OpenHands + Devstral-Small-2-24B (baseline): 34.3%; 175; 3.94M
- Raw trace + OpenHands + Devstral-Small-2-24B: 49.2% (+14.9, p<.001); 73 (-58%); 1.66M (-58%)
- Summary notes + OpenHands + Devstral-Small-2-24B: 43.6% (+9.4, p=0.005); 123 (-30%); 2.30M (-42%)
- Structured notes + OpenHands + Devstral-Small-2-24B: 44.8% (+10.5, p<.001); 125 (-29%); 2.30M (-42%)
Robustness (Qwen->Qwen, 40 points x 3 repeats, events/tokens only): repo only 102.5 events, 1.62M; raw trace 42 (-59%), 906k; summary 52 (-49%), 591k; structured 58 (-43%), 677k (Table 4). Predecessor robustness (Devstral successor): Gemma and Devstral predecessors also show 21-46% event reductions (Table 6)
Verdicts: quality and cost: no criterion stated by the authors (all configurations)

fields.v: Tasks: 75 SWE-bench Verified source tasks (seed 20260430) -> 181 handoff points. Configurations: 4 handoff views x 3 successor models (Qwen, Gemma, Devstral), predecessor fixed to Qwen. Baseline: repository only. Held constant: predecessor, handoff point, checkpointed repository, successor model, runtime, takeover instruction block, serving configuration. Acceptance tests: official SWE-bench held-out tests. Repetitions: 1 per handoff point and view in main study; robustness subset 3 repeats; second robustness with 3 predecessors (6,120 runs). Human intervention: none

Cost: all context-bearing views cut median agent events (raw trace -57 to -59%, notes -20 to -46%) and prompt tokens (-42 to -63%) vs repository only; all matched bootstrap CIs below zero. Quality: raw trace +6.1 to +14.9 pp (significant for all three successors); notes +1.1 to +5.0 pp for Qwen and Gemma (not significant), +9.4/+10.5 pp for Devstral (significant). No single best view across successors; summary vs structured notes similar. Raw trace first prompt median 87k chars vs 7.2k (repo), 9.8k (summary), 10.0k (structured). Largest gains at 'after first post-failure edit' (+12.9 pp Qwen, +19.4 pp Devstral). Small negative deltas for Gemma note views in 'needs completion' state. No multiple-comparison correction

Distinguished views clearly on cost (events, tokens), less on solved rate (model-dependent, often n.s.). Repeatability: robustness rerun (3 attempts, 40 points) and predecessor-robustness study reproduce the efficiency pattern. Limitations stated: one runtime (OpenHands-style); single run per handoff point in main study; 75 source tasks; SWE-bench validation does not cover maintainability or human usefulness; no multiple-comparison correction

Conclusions limited to one OpenHands-style runtime (absolute counts may change elsewhere); single-run handoffs in main study; 75 source tasks; validation covers patch correctness only, not maintainability or human usefulness. Gaps: benchmarks should report handoff debt alongside resolution; agent systems should make handoff output a deliberate part of the workflow; protocol could evaluate adaptive memory policies

Code public: github.com/anjilab/agent-handoff-debt. No pre-registration. Language: Python (SWE-bench). Open-weight models served locally via vLLM on NVIDIA RTX PRO 6000 GPUs; model identifiers Qwen/Qwen3.6-27B, google/gemma-4-31B-it, mistralai/Devstral-Small-2-24B-Instruct-2512.
